fixes.row: A life for a life; a ransom
fixes.why: The row heading says life-for-life and ransom. John 10:11-18, 15:13 and 1 John 3:16 say 'lay down' and never use ransom or exchange language (15:13 is 'for his friends', 1 John 3:16 'for the brothers'). Filing them under the ransom heading, beside the census ransom and the lex talionis, reads a substitution/ransom frame into them. The note then says the page takes no side, but the grouping has already chosen. The same John verses are also the examples of the 'laid down' row, so one verse sits in two rows. Also, the census ransom (Exod 30:12-16) is protective, not a penalty, and the law of 'life for life' is an equal-penalty rule; they are different laws and the text does not say the later ransom saying is any of them.
fixes.fix: Keep in this row only the verses that carry a price or an equal-for-equal exchange: Exod 21:23, 21:30, 30:12, 30:15-16, Lev 24:18, Deut 19:21, Num 35:31, Isa 43:4, Matt 20:28, Mark 10:45 (and Isa 53:12 only with a note that it says 'poured out His life'). Remove John 10:11, 10:15, 10:17, 10:18, 15:13 and 1 John 3:16 and leave them in 'A life laid down'. Relabel 'A life given in exchange: "life for life", "a ransom for his life", "a ransom for many"'. Add to the note that these are separate laws and sayings, and that the text itself does not say Matt 20:28 refers back to Exod 30.

fixes.row: A life laid down, lost, saved, sought, spared or loved
fixes.why: About two thirds of the 47 verses are the Hebrew idiom of enemies 'seeking' someone's life (Saul and David, the psalmists, Jeremiah), a different thing from a person laying down or losing his own life. The label and the first example lead with John 10:11 and Mark 8:35, so the Old Testament idiom is filed under the New Testament sayings. Also the row promises 'spared' but Gen 12:13, Gen 19:17-20, 1 Sam 26:21, Esth 7:3, Job 2:4-6 and Luke 17:33 (the same saying as Mark 8:35 and Matt 10:39) are in 'Every other use'.
fixes.fix: Split into two: (a) 'A life sought, taken, spared or saved' with the Hebrew idiom first (1 Kgs 19:10, 1 Sam 20:1, 22:23, 23:15, 25:29, Ps 35:4, 38:12, 40:14, 54:3, 63:9, 70:2, 86:14, Jer 4:30, 11:21, 19:7, 19:9, 21:7, 22:25, 34:20-21, 44:30, 46:26, 49:37; add from the catch-all Gen 12:13, 19:17-20, Job 2:4-6, Esth 7:3, 1 Sam 26:21) with Mark 3:4 and Luke 6:9; (b) 'A life laid down, lost, saved for His sake' (Matt 10:39, 16:25, Mark 8:35, Luke 9:24, 14:26, 17:33, John 10:11-18, 12:25, 13:37-38, 15:13, 1 John 3:16, Rev 12:11, 1 Pet 3:10). Move Luke 17:33 into (b).

fixes.row: The breath of life; the Spirit of life
fixes.why: One row with the Holy Spirit as a door puts Genesis 2:7 and 7:22 (breath given to all flesh, animals included) under the same heading and door as Rom 8:2, 8:6 and John 6:63. The Hebrew of Genesis has no 'spirit' in 2:7 and the creatures of 7:22 are not given the Holy Spirit; the label 'Spirit of life' with that door reads the later Pauline term back into Genesis. The worker says it did not decide breath versus Spirit, but a joined label and a Holy Spirit door do decide it. It is also a divine-person door attached by rule to a mixed row. Rom 8:6 ('the mind of the Spirit is life and peace') is not the same kind of saying as the others and also sits in 'Life set beside death'.
fixes.fix: Split. Row 'The breath of life' (Gen 2:7, 6:17, 7:15, 7:22, Job 12:10, Acts 17:25, Rev 11:11), door breath_of_life only, note: 'In Genesis the word is breath; the page does not say it is the Spirit.' Row 'The Spirit and life' (Rom 8:2, 8:6, John 6:63, with 2 Cor 3:6 and 1 Cor 15:45 moved from the verb row only if Doug wants them by hand), door holy_ghost, note that the Spirit is named in these verses only. Remove the holy_ghost door from the Genesis row.

fixes.row: Eternal life, said as had or given now
fixes.why: John 5:39 is Jesus' report of what his opponents suppose ('you think that in them you have eternal life'); filing it as evidence of eternal life 'had now' gives them a claim Jesus does not endorse. John 6:54 is also in 'Now and later in the same verse', so the same verse is both in the 'now' row and the 'both' row. John 6:40 in the 'both' row reads 'shall have' (the same ambiguity the worker used to keep 3:15-16, 5:40 and 20:31 out of all three rows), so the principle is applied unevenly. Splitting 'have' into now/later at all is the reader's decision that the Greek present or subjunctive carries time, when the text often does not; the worker's own note admits it. The side-by-side arrangement of John 3:16 (own_words) cannot be found on the page at all, since it is in 'Every other use'.
fixes.fix: Drop John 5:39 from the row (or keep it with a note naming the speaker's opponents). Take John 6:54 out of 'now' and leave it in 'Now and later'. Move John 6:40 out of 'Now and later' into a small fourth row 'Eternal life with "shall have" or "may have": John 3:15, 3:16, 3:36 context, 5:40, 6:40, 20:31, 1 Tim 1:16' with the same no-side note and the three-row cross-reference. Then John 3:16 is findable.

fixes.row: Now and later in the same verse: "has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day"; "in this age ... in the age to come"
fixes.why: Rom 6:22 ('the fruit you get leads to holiness, and the outcome is eternal life') names a result, not a now and a later in one sentence. Luke 18:30 and Mark 10:30 set 'many times as much in this age' (goods and kin) beside 'eternal life' in the age to come; that is not life 'now' (the reward now is not life). John 12:25 ('in this world... keep it for eternal life') has life only once. The label promises two time markers on the same life and these three do not give that.
fixes.fix: Move Rom 6:22 to the 'still to come' row (as 'the outcome'); relabel the row 'Two times in one verse' and keep Mark 10:30 and Luke 18:30 with a one-line note that the present-age reward there is houses and kin, with eternal life in the age to come; keep John 6:54, 1 Tim 4:8; move John 12:25 to the 'laid down' row.

fixes.row: Eternal life, said as still to come
fixes.why: Dan 12:2 is the only Hebrew Scripture verse and the row is headed by the later New Testament term 'eternal life'; the Hebrew is life of the age (chayyei olam), awakening from the dust. It is a different book, century and phrase from Matthew's 'inherit eternal life'. Acts 13:46 ('you judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life') does not say the life is yet to come, only that it is offered now.
fixes.fix: Add to the note: 'Dan 12:2 is the Hebrew Bible's own wording (life of the age, after waking from the dust) and is set first, as written, not as the New Testament idea.' Move Acts 13:46 to the 'shall have/may have' row or out of this row.

fixes.row: Christ and life: "I am the life", "the resurrection and the life", "the Author of life", "Christ, who is your life", "newness of life", "life in His Son"
fixes.why: The label puts 'newness of life' (Rom 6:4) among the sayings about Christ's own life, though that verse is about the believer's walk. 1 John 5:20 ('He is the true God and eternal life') depends on whom 'He' is; the page says divine persons are by hand, yet it is in the row without a note. At the same time John 1:4 ('In Him was life'), the foundation of this whole line of John and the clearest statement of the arc Genesis 2:7, John 1:4, 1 John 1:1-2, Rev 22:1, is left in the 208-verse 'Every other use' with a note. A reader looking for what the Bible says of Christ and life would not look there. The arc of life in John (1:4, 5:26, 6:35, 11:25, 14:6, 20:31) is cut apart from its first verse.
fixes.fix: Put John 1:4, 1 John 1:1-2 into this row (or a one-line row 'The life that was with the Father') on Doug's per-record decision, keeping the note that the verses say 'Him' and 'the Word'. Add a note to 1 John 5:20 that 'He' may refer to the Son or the Father and the page takes no side. Move Rom 6:4 ('newness of life') to the 'To live to God' verb row or the believer's-life row.

fixes.row: A fountain, a spring, water, bread, light "of life"; called "living": water, bread, a sacrifice, a hope, stones, a way, the word of God
fixes.why: One 30-verse row joins two phrases the label itself marks: 'of life' (Hebrew chayyim, Greek zoe: fountain of life, light of life) and 'called living' (Hebrew chay, Greek zao: living water, living sacrifice, living stones, living hope, living way, living oracles). The label does not say these are different words, and the row title is the longest in the hub. The Hebrew fountain-of-life sayings (Psalm 36:9, Proverbs, Jeremiah 2:13) are the source of the figure and are mixed in the first examples with John 4 and 6. Also Prov 10:11, 13:14, 14:27 and 16:22 are the same kind of saying as the 'path of life' row and could belong there.
fixes.fix: Split into 'A fountain, a spring of life' (Ps 36:9, Prov 10:11, 13:14, 14:27, 16:22, Prov 4:23, Jer 2:13, 17:13, Zech 14:8, Rev 7:17, 21:6, 22:1, 22:17), 'Living water, the bread of life, the light of life' (John 4:10-14, 6:33-51, 7:38, 8:12) and 'Called "living": a sacrifice, hope, stones, a way, the word of God' (Rom 12:1, 1 Pet 1:3, 1:23, 2:4-5, Heb 4:12, 10:20, Acts 7:38), each with a one-line note that the Hebrew chayyim and the Greek zao are different words. Or, if the count must fall, keep one row but shorten the title to 'A fountain, water, bread, light of life; and things called "living"' and add the note.

fixes.row: The days of life, the years of life, a lifetime, a long life
fixes.why: 1 Kgs 3:11, 2 Chr 1:11, Job 12:12 and Ps 91:16 are in this row and also in the 'others' list as the Hebrew yom (day), with a note that 'the page does not make the two one'. They cannot be in both. If they are here because the same verse also contains a life-word (e.g. nephesh in 'life of your enemies'), the row label 'a long life' is not what that word is doing. Gen 47:28 is in this row and also in 'The years one lived' (verb), a second doubling.
fixes.fix: Remove 1 Kgs 3:11, 2 Chr 1:11, Job 12:12, Ps 91:16 from this row and leave them in 'others' with their note (or keep them here only with an in-row note saying the Hebrew is 'length of days'). Remove Gen 47:28 from one of the two lifespan rows.

fixes.why: Gen 7:4 is in this row yet 'others' lists it under yequm (existence) with Gen 7:23 as a different word. The note says 'the same Hebrew word' for Gen 1 and Ezekiel; that is true for chayyah, but the Genesis 'living creature' is nephesh chayyah and the row sits within a hub where nephesh is read 'life only'. Rule 4 needs one word per statement. Placing the Ezekiel visionary creatures with animals is on the same word and is a legitimate echo, but the row title makes the visionary beings 'living things' alike.
fixes.fix: Remove Gen 7:4 from the row (it is yequm). Reword the note: 'The Hebrew chayyah is the word for the animals of Gen 1 and for the four "living creatures" of Ezekiel 1 and 10; the visionary beings are not said to be animals, and the page does not say what they are.'

fixes.row: The dead live again: "will live", "came to life", "was dead and has come to life", "alive"
fixes.why: The heading puts several different things together. Rev 13:14 (the beast 'wounded by the sword and yet lived') is not a resurrection of the dead in the sense of the others and its place beside Christ's resurrection hands the reader a parallel the text may intend as parody but the page asserts. Luke 15:24 and 15:32 are a parable figure for a lost son. Matt 9:18, Acts 9:41 and Acts 20:12 are a raising or a revival the narrator reports as an event. Ezekiel 37 is explained in the chapter as Israel. The label 'the dead live again' flattens a literal raising, a figure and a vision. 'Alive' in the label is a word with no verse.
fixes.fix: Relabel 'The dead made to live, and the figure of it'. Move Rev 13:14 to a one-line 'beast' note in the catch-all or keep with a note that the verse is about the beast and the page does not say it is parallel to the raisings. Add to the note that Luke 15:24 and 15:32 are the father's words of his son in a parable. Optionally split: 'Raised in the narrative' (1 Kgs 17:22, 2 Kgs 13:21, Matt 9:18, Mark 5:23, Acts 9:41, 20:12), 'The vision and the promise' (Ezek 37, Isa 26:19, Job 14:14, Hos 6:2, John 5:25), 'Christ, who was dead and lives' (Rev 1:18, 2:8, Rom 14:9, 2 Cor 13:4, Luke 24:5, Acts 1:3, 25:19).

fixes.row: Revive: "revive me", "give me life", "You will revive me", "He will revive us", "revive the heart of the contrite"
fixes.why: This row and 'God makes alive' use the same Hebrew verb (chayah in the piel) with the same agent. The split rests only on the Berean's English ('revive' versus 'give life'). The nine-fold 'revive me' prayer of Psalm 119 is the Old Testament's own repeated version of 'the LORD gives life' in 1 Sam 2:6 and Deut 32:39; splitting them cuts apart what belongs together and gives a reader of Ps 119 no sign that the text says God is the giver of life there as well. It also lets 'make alive' read as a New Testament idea (Eph 2:5, Col 2:13) with the Old Testament set apart as 'revive'.
fixes.fix: Merge into 'God makes alive, revives, gives life' with Deut 32:39, 1 Sam 2:6, Neh 9:6, Job 33:4 first, then Ps 119 and Hos 6:2, then the New Testament; keep both existing notes. This also drops the row count by one.

fixes.row: Live by the commandments: "the man who does these things will live by them", "Do this and you will live", "live by every word"
fixes.why: The note introduces the next row 'as Gal 3:11-12 sets them' and then lists four Christian ways of reading the law (way of life, guide, schoolmaster, ended). That puts Paul's contrast onto Lev 18:5 and Hab 2:4, which do not mention each other, and every named reading is a Christian reading of the Torah, none is the Torah's own sense (that obeying the commandments is how Israel is to live in the land, Deut 30:15-20). The row is Hebrew-first by order but the note is not. Deut 8:3 'live on every word' is about bread and manna, a different saying, and sits in the row only through Matt 4:4.
fixes.fix: Rewrite the note: 'In Lev 18:5, Deut 4:1, 5:33, 8:1, 30:16 and Ezek 20 the commandments are given so that Israel may live. Paul quotes Lev 18:5 in Gal 3:12 and Rom 10:5 beside Hab 2:4 in a contrast the verses themselves set; the page lists the Hebrew first, as written, and takes no side on how Christian traditions relate the two.' Drop 'as ended' to a clause attributed to a reading, or keep all the readings and add 'and as the law is read in Jewish tradition, as the way Israel lives'.

fixes.row: Life held out: "the promise: eternal life", "the crown of life", "the word of life", "the full message of this new life", "the gracious gift of life", "the life of God"
fixes.why: 'Held out' is the page's own category, not the text's. Eph 4:18 ('alienated from the life of God') says the reverse of held out. 1 Pet 3:7 'gracious gift of life' is addressed to husbands about wives as co-heirs. Crown of life (Jas 1:12, Rev 2:10) is a future reward, and so belongs beside the 'still to come' row; placing it separately means the 'to come' row is thinner than the text and the page chooses where 'promise' goes.
fixes.fix: Relabel 'Phrases with "life": the promise of eternal life, the crown of life, the word of life, the gift of life'. Move Eph 4:18 to the catch-all (or a note). Add a note that Jas 1:12 and Rev 2:10 are also set beside the 'still to come' row.

fixes.row: Oath by a life: "As surely as the LORD lives", "as surely as I live", "as surely as you live", "as surely as Pharaoh lives"
fixes.why: Ps 18:46 and 2 Sam 22:47 ('The LORD lives! Blessed be my Rock') are a cry of praise, not an oath formula. Amos 8:14 and Hos 4:15 quote the formula in the mouths of idolaters ('as your god lives'), not the LORD's own oath-taking. Rom 14:11 quotes the formula (from Isa 49:18, 45:23) in a different book. The label says all of the 77 are oaths.
fixes.fix: Move Ps 18:46 and 2 Sam 22:47 to 'The living God; He who lives forever'. Add a note: 'Most are oaths by the LORD's life, by the speaker's own life or by a king's; Amos 8:14 and Hos 4:15 are the formula used of other gods or in false worship.'

fixes.why: 413 of the hub's 1,088 verses (38%) are in the two catch-alls. The noun catch-all holds John 3:16 (one of the hub's own key verses) and John 1:4, Luke 17:33 (the twin of Mark 8:35), Ezek 32:23-27 ('terror in the land of the living', the same phrase as the row that holds Ezek 32:32 and 26:20), and a group of prayers 'deliver my life / save my life' (Ps 6:4, 22:20, 25:20, 33:19, 56:13) and 'spare his life' (Gen 12:13, Job 2:4-6, Esth 7:3, 1 Sam 26:21) that the 'laid down... spared' label promises. A reader scanning for 'what does Ezekiel say of the land of the living' gets part of it in the row and part in the catch-all.
fixes.fix: Move Ezek 32:23-27 to 'Alive, and the living'; Luke 17:33 to the laid-down row; Gen 12:13, Job 2:4-6, Esth 7:3, 1 Sam 26:21 to the 'spared' row; John 3:15-16 to the new 'shall have / may have' row; John 1:4 per the Christ-row fix. Add a row 'Deliver my life: prayers for a life kept from death' (Ps 6:4, 22:20, 25:20, 33:19, 56:13, 86:2, 116:4, 119:109, Jonah 2:7, Lam 3:58).

fixes.why: Dozens of verses appear in two rows or both lists: the 'living God' verses are in the noun row and again in the verb catch-all; 'living water' (John 4:10-11, 7:38), 'living bread' (6:51) and 'living sacrifice' (Rom 12:1) are in the noun 'fountain' row and again in the verb catch-all. The report calls this 'cross-form picks' (a participle counted as a verb), but a reader sees the same verse twice with no explanation, and the verb catch-all's first example is Matt 16:16.
fixes.fix: Add one sentence in the verb catch-all note: 'The participle "living" (the living God, living water) is listed in the noun rows and is repeated here only where the verb is not elsewhere shown.' Or remove from the verb catch-all every verse already in a noun row.

fixes.row: To live to God, to righteousness, for the Lord, with Christ, by the Spirit: "because I live, you also will live"
fixes.why: 1 Pet 4:6 ('the gospel was preached even to those who are dead, that they might live according to God in the spirit') is one of the most disputed verses for Christian traditions (who the dead are, when it was preached) and has no note. John 6:57 'the living Father sent Me' is a divine title, not a believer living to God, and belongs in 'The living God'. John 6:58 ('will live forever') is life without the 'to God/for the Lord' notion. 2 Tim 3:12 and Titus 2:12 are 'live godly', a manner, not a dedication.
fixes.fix: Add a note to 1 Pet 4:6: 'Readers differ on who the dead are and when the gospel was preached to them; the page takes no side.' Move John 6:57 (first clause) to the living-God row; John 6:58 to 'God makes alive' or the 'shall have' row.

fixes.why: Count only: the hub shows 32 rows against a brief of about 15-25. This row and 'The present life' both treat life as short or burdensome; merging is possible, but the lament is a distinct voice in Job, Jonah and Elijah and the worker is right to keep it. Gen 27:46 is Rebekah's pretext to Isaac, not despair, so the 'weary' label is the speaker's words, not her state.
fixes.fix: Keep the row, but add the note 'Rebekah says it to move Isaac to send Jacob away (Gen 27:46); the page lists it as she says it.' To cut count instead, merge 'Livelihood' into 'The present life' with a note that it is the Greek bios, and fold 'Life held out' into 'Phrases with life' per the other fix.

worker_points.point: Eternal life now / to come / both: three rows, none tilted
worker_points.why: Three rows still decide that 'have' is a tense. John 5:39 is the opponents' presumption, John 6:54 and 6:40 are in both rows, Rom 6:22 and Luke 18:30 do not show a now and a later, and John 3:15-16 (the hub's key verse) cannot be found at all because it is in the catch-all. See the fixes. The notes and the no-side wording are good.

worker_points.point: Acts 13:48 'appointed for eternal life' placed in the 'still to come' row with a note
worker_points.why: The note names both readings (God's choice, or those disposed) and the verse is shown as written. Acts 13:46 beside it is the one to move.

worker_points.point: Live by the commandments beside live by faith
worker_points.why: Order is Hebrew first and the verses are as written, but the note adopts Gal 3:11-12's contrast and names only Christian readings. See the note fix. The rabbi's seat should read this row.

worker_points.point: The book of life: Ps 69:28 and Rev 3:5 beside Rev 13:8 and 17:8
worker_points.why: Both sides are shown and the note takes no side. Add that the Hebrew roots (Exod 32:32-33 'blot me out of Your book', Dan 12:1, Mal 3:16) belong beside it. Rev 22:19 (tree of life) carries a known textual variant (book of life) in some manuscripts and could carry a note.

worker_points.point: The dead live again (Ezek 37, Rev 20:4-5, Job 14:14, Isa 26:19, Hos 6:2)
worker_points.why: The notes are even-handed but the row mixes narrative raisings, a parable (Luke 15), a vision, the beast (Rev 13:14) and Christ's resurrection under one label. Hos 6:2 is in 'Revive', not here, while Ezek 37 is here; the same type of verse is filed in two rows.

worker_points.point: God makes alive (1 Cor 15:22, Eph 2:5, Col 2:13, John 5:21 by hand)
worker_points.why: The notes take no side on 'all' or on new life versus resurrection. 1 Pet 3:18 'made alive by the Spirit' (spirit or Spirit) should get a note, as the Holy Spirit door sits on the row. And the row should merge with 'Revive'.

worker_points.point: Christ and life, selected by hand; John 1:4 and 1 John 1:1-2 left in the catch-all
worker_points.why: The hand rule is right but leaves John 1:4, the hub's most important Christ-and-life verse, in a 208-verse unlabelled row. Needs Doug's per-record decision on moving them. John 6:53 with its note is fine.

worker_points.point: A life for a life; a ransom
worker_points.why: John 10:11-18, 15:13 and 1 John 3:16 are in the ransom row without ransom language, and the same verses are in the 'laid down' row. The note takes no side but the grouping does. See the first fix.

worker_points.point: The life is in the blood (Lev 17:11 shown, atonement deferred)
worker_points.why: The label is Lev 17:11, 17:14 and Deut 12:23 as written; the note on 'lifeblood' for Gen 9:4-5 is exact and the page defers atonement to the blood card. Nothing is added.

worker_points.point: Rom 5:18 in the catch-all and Prov 8:35 in 'The path of life' with notes
worker_points.why: Both notes take no side. Rom 5:18 would be easier to find in the 'still to come' or the 'Christ' row but its place is not wrong.

worker_points.point: Breath of life / Spirit of life not decided
worker_points.why: A joined label and a Holy Spirit door do decide it. See the split fix.

worker_points.point: Weary of life: hard verses kept
worker_points.why: Honest and useful. Add a note on Gen 27:46.

worker_points.point: Words and others: חָיָה and ζῳοποιέω taken in as the same family; ζῷον and יוֹם kept apart
worker_points.why: The family argument (the Greek Old Testament renders chayah by zao and zoopoieo) is sound and the others list with notes is correct practice. Fix the duplicated yom verses and Gen 7:4 (yequm).

Over by seven. Merges that cost nothing: Revive into God makes alive; Life held out relabelled and folded into a phrases row; Livelihood noted into the present life row. The 413 verses in catch-alls are a larger problem than the count.

missing.what: The living praise the LORD, and the dead do not: an Old Testament row of the living as those who give thanks (all now in the catch-alls or scattered).
To keep alive and let live: the midwives, Joseph's 'to preserve life', Rahab, the Gibeonites, the law's 'so that you may live'. A story-arc row from the catch-all.
The Hebrew roots of the book of life, which have no life-word but are the same figure: names written in or blotted from God's book.

examples_checked: 30 of 32 rows' four examples show their label as the Berean prints them (32 rows including 2 catch-alls); the two catch-alls' own first examples (Luke 17:33 and Matt 16:16) belong in labelled rows, and one example, Gen 3:5 'was 130 years old' (Gen 5:3), shows the Berean's wording, not 'lived', as the label says it will
summary: The hub is true to the text in most rows and its no-side notes are careful, but the ransom row files John's 'lay down' verses under a ransom heading, the 'seeking a life' and the Genesis breath verses sit under New Testament headings, and 413 verses (38%) are left in two catch-alls that hold verses the labelled rows promise, including John 3:16 and John 1:4. Ship after the ransom, breath/Spirit, eternal-life-now and laid-down rows are fixed, the yom and yequm verses are taken out of the main rows, and the catch-alls are emptied of what the labels already claim.
